title: Writing and Comparing Fractions · Sean’s Gifts
subject: Word Problems

match.first: What fraction of the gifts are train sets?

items.prompt: What fraction of the gifts are train sets?

steps.why: The part is the train sets. The whole is all the gifts he received.
A fraction compares the part to the whole. The toy box numbers are not part of the gifts.
3 of the 20 gifts are train sets. It cannot be simplified.

items.context: Sean had 3 building sets and 18 toy cars in his toy box. At his birthday party, he received 20 gifts. He got 3 train sets, 4 building sets and 9 toy cars. The rest of the gifts are comic books. 3/4 of the gifts are wrapped. 13/15 of the wrapped gifts are wrapped in blue wrapping paper and 1/5 of them are wrapped with ribbons.

items.prompt: What fraction of the gifts are comic books?

steps.why: The comic books are “the rest”. Add the other gifts, then take that from 20.
mark: The rest of the gifts are comic books

steps.why: Train sets, building sets and toy cars are 16 gifts.
Take the 16 other gifts away from all 20.
4 out of 20 simplified by dividing the top and bottom by 4. Answer: 4/20, or 1/5.

items.context: Sean had 3 building sets and 18 toy cars in his toy box. At his birthday party, he received 20 gifts. He got 3 train sets, 4 building sets and 9 toy cars. The rest of the gifts are comic books. 3/4 of the gifts are wrapped. 13/15 of the wrapped gifts are wrapped in blue wrapping paper and 1/5 of them are wrapped with ribbons.

items.prompt: What fraction of his toy cars are new?

steps.work: Numbers: 18 toy cars before, 9 toy cars received
steps.why: New cars are the ones he got as gifts. All his cars are the old ones plus the new ones.
The whole is every toy car he has now.
9 of his 27 toy cars are new.
Divide the top and bottom by 9. Answer: 9/27, or 1/3.

items.prompt: What fraction of his building sets are old?

steps.why: Old building sets are the ones he already had. The new ones came as gifts.
The whole is every building set he has now.
3 of his 7 building sets are old.
It cannot be simplified because 3 and 7 share no factor but 1.

items.context: Sean had 3 building sets and 18 toy cars in his toy box. At his birthday party, he received 20 gifts. He got 3 train sets, 4 building sets and 9 toy cars. The rest of the gifts are comic books. 3/4 of the gifts are wrapped. 13/15 of the wrapped gifts are wrapped in blue wrapping paper and 1/5 of them are wrapped with ribbons.

items.prompt: Are there more gifts that are wrapped or more gifts that are unwrapped?
items.answer: Since there are 3/4 of the gifts wrapped, there are more gift wrapped than gifts that are unwrapped.

steps.why: This is the fraction we need. The rest of the gifts are unwrapped.
The whole is 4 out of 4. Take away the wrapped part.
The bottoms are the same, so the bigger top wins. 3 is more than 1.
3/4 is more than 1/4 of the gifts.

items.context: Sean had 3 building sets and 18 toy cars in his toy box. At his birthday party, he received 20 gifts. He got 3 train sets, 4 building sets and 9 toy cars. The rest of the gifts are comic books. 3/4 of the gifts are wrapped. 13/15 of the wrapped gifts are wrapped in blue wrapping paper and 1/5 of them are wrapped with ribbons.

items.prompt: Are there more gifts wrapped in blue wrapping paper or more gift wrapped with ribbons?
items.answer: Since 1/5 < 13/15, there are more gifts wrapped in blue wrapping paper.

steps.why: Compare these two fractions. Both are parts of the wrapped gifts.
5 goes into 15, so use 15 for both fractions.
Multiply the top and bottom of 1/5 by 3.
3 is less than 13, so more gifts are wrapped in blue paper.
